Title: BMI retreat strengthens strategy for brain health and resilience
NewsSummary: Staff and community partners chart the future of research on aging and dementia
NewsContent:
​The Brain and Mind Institute’s (BMI) Brain Health Research team hosted its Joint Planning and Strategy Retreat in Nyahururu, Kenya, from August 20–22, 2025. Held under the theme Advancing Brain Health Together, the retreat brought together researchers and Community Advisory Board members to review progress, refine strategies and build stronger collaborations for the future of brain health in Kenya and beyond.

The retreat spotlighted BMI’s diverse research portfolio, including Brain Resilience Kenya, Africa-FINGERS, BRIDGE Africa (Bridging Research Infrastructure for Dementia Gaps in East Africa), and FeMBER Africa (Female Brain Health and Endocrine Research in Africa). Discussions focused on community engagement, data readiness, publication capacity, and ethics, pillars seen as essential for impactful brain health research.

Dr. Chi Udeh-Momoh, Translational Neuroscientist at BMI and Principal Investigator across the projects, stressed the significance of the gathering. “We are at a critical moment where we are collecting incredible, cutting-edge data that can help us understand not only the risks of pathological aging but also the factors that support resilience. At BMI, we work in true partnership with communities to co-design strategies that are both effective and sustainable. What we discover here in Africa will shape solutions not only for our continent, but for the world,” she said.

A key focus was community participation, reflecting BMI’s Living Lab model, which emphasizes co-creation, dialogue and testing solutions in real-world settings. This approach ensures that interventions remain relevant and sustainable.

Catherine Bikeri, Brain Resilience Kenya Project Manager, highlighted the importance of listening to the people most affected. “Community voices are central to our work. This retreat allowed us to reflect on how we engage and ensure research meaningfully benefits the people. In doing so, we strengthen trust and build truly sustainable solutions,” she said.

What stood out throughout the retreat was the recognition that African-led science is shaping global understanding of brain health. By producing knowledge grounded in local realities and addressing challenges unique to the continent, BMI and its partners are positioning Africa as a driver of global innovation in brain health, healthy aging and resilience.

The gathering closed with a renewed commitment to accountability, ethical integrity and collaboration. More than a review of progress, it laid the foundation for new strategies to advance BMI’s mission, ensuring African-led solutions remain at the forefront in the fight against dementia and in promoting brain resilience across communities.
